name: Diethylcarbamazine

overview.mechanism: Diethylcarbamazine citrate is microfilaricidal and active against adult lymphatic filarial worms [[DECCDC]].
uses: CDC identifies diethylcarbamazine as treatment for lymphatic filariasis; established late chronic disease is not reversed by antiparasitic treatment [[DECCDC]].

sources.citation: FDA Philippines product-registration data preserved in the website registry; exact generic/product records inspected November 25, 2026. Cached record, not a new verification of current registration validity.
CDC. Clinical Treatment of Lymphatic Filariasis. Verified November 25, 2026. US clinical guidance, not a Philippine Filrezin product insert.

Adjepon-Yamoah KK, Edwards G, Breckenridge AM, Orme ML, Ward SA. The effect of renal disease on the pharmacokinetics of diethylcarbamazine in man. Br J Clin Pharmacol.1982; 13(6):829–834. PMID 7093114.

draft_notes: No inferred CKD-band, HD, PD or CRRT regimen. Current Philippine product identity/insert governs applicability.

revision_log.change: Source-verified descriptive evidence and explicitly attributed regulatory guidance; numerical recommended doses only from verified exact local insert.
revision_log.approved_by: W. G. M. Rivero, MD (delegated source-verification workflow; executed by Codex, 2026-11-25)

usual_adult_dose.dose: No numerical Filrezin regimen assigned: the exact local insert was not verified. Treatment indication, parasite exposure and kidney function require assessment [[PHREG,DECCDC,DECPK]]

contraindications: CDC: contraindicated when concomitant onchocerciasis is possible; exclude it with a consistent exposure history because severe skin/eye reactions can occur [[DECCDC]]

common: Dizziness, nausea, fever, headache, muscle or joint pain; reactions depend partly on circulating microfilarial burden [[DECCDC]]
serious: With high circulating Loa loa burden, life-threatening encephalopathy and renal failure can occur [[DECCDC]]

monitoring: CDC advises extreme caution and tropical-medicine consultation with high Loa loa microfilarial burden; steroids or slow dose escalation do not prevent these severe complications [[DECCDC]]

evidence.title: Product identity and renal evidence
evidence.intro: No modern dialysis regimen is established by this old pharmacokinetic study.

rows.intervention: Diethylcarbamazine citrate 50 mg(unbranded DR-XY 43355; Filrezin DR-XY 44594) and Filrezin 100 mg(DR-XY 44892).
rows.findings: These are citrate-tablet records; tablet strength does not supply an indication-specific regimen.
rows.limitations: CDC guidance is not an exact Philippine insert; no current US-label import made.

rows.design: 12 patients with chronic kidney-function impairment; PK correlations with creatinine clearance.
rows.findings: Lower creatinine clearance was associated with longer half-life; impaired participants had increased half-life/AUC and reduced 24-hour urinary excretion. Excretion also tended to decrease with increasing urinary pH.
rows.limitations: Small historical PK study; no numerical CKD adjustment or HD/PD/CRRT schedule inferred. CrCl is not relabeled eGFR.

renal: A 12-patient chronic-renal-impairment study found increased half-life/AUC and reduced urinary excretion; creatinine clearance was associated with elimination [[DECPK]].
This historical PK study does not establish a numerical CKD reduction or HD, PD or CRRT regimen; no Filrezin adjustment is inferred [[DECPK]].
